newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C AMATIL SEES PHILIPPINE ECONOMIC GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: C-C AMATIL SEES PHILIPPINE ECONOMIC GROWTH.

text.p: Strong economic growth in the Philippines would assist efforts to boost soft-drink consumption in Coca-Cola Amatil's single biggest market, the bottler's managing director, Norb Cole, said on Thursday.
C-C Amatil currently has about 75 percent of the Philippines market, where per capita consumption of Coca-Cola products is around 122 serves a year, compared with about 320 in Australia.

"The real opportunity for us in the Philippines is not to grow market share ... but to grow the total market," Cole said in answer to questions after an address to the Securities Institute of Australia.
"And the way to grow the total market is to grow per capita consumption," Cole added.

The Philippines has become the Australian-based bottler's biggest single market following the acquisition of the soft-drink operations of San Miguel Corp in a A$3.4 billion share swap deal last April.
C-C Amatil incorporated three months of the Philippine unit's operations in its half year report released on Wednesday, boosting interim net profit by A$40 million to A$98.1 million.

The Philippines contributed sales revenue of A$354.4 million and a A$64.8 million trading profit in three months, compared with sales revenue of A$1.87 billion and a trading profit of A$163.6 million over six months from all other operations.
Cole pointed to economic growth in the Philippines, which he said was running at six-to-eight percent, and the sharp rise in per capita income, currently around US$1,300.
"Per capita income is going up rapidly, which means an increase in disposable income, which means more money to buy discretionary disposable items," he said.
Cole said the "economic pyramid" in the Philippines was also very steep with many people earning less than US$200 a year.
"As those people move up the pyramid you effectively have new people coming into the market," he said.
The Philippines unit has 21 plants, 15,000 employees, 500,000 sales outlets and serves a market of 70 million people.
Cole said a recent inspection of the plants had shown they were extremely well maintained, and future capital requirements would be within a normal range.
Sales volumes in the Philippines reached an all-time record April and May and the strong growth continued in July, he said.
For the quarter to end-June, sales volumes rose 19 percent and the unit delivered a trading profit margin of 18.3 percent, down from 20 percent earlier.
Cole said the fall from 20 percent had been flagged in the independent expert's report into the Philippines' purchase.
The Philippines would deliver acceptable margins in the second half, but he declined to indicate a figure.
"What we had was 19 percent volume growth and 18 percent margins," Cole said. "It's a great combination. We would like to replicate that all over the world."
